claim: Long title of the Act: 'An Act to provide for compensation to the States for the loss of revenue arising on account of implementation of the goods and services tax in pursuance of the provisions of the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016.' Assent 12 April 2017.
source: GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 (Act 15 of 2017, assent 12 Apr 2017), text on CBIC GST site
second_source: Same Act, PDF on the GST Council site

claim: Section 18 of the 101st Amendment Act: Parliament shall by law, on the Council's recommendation, provide compensation to States for loss of revenue from GST 'for a period of five years'.
source: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II s.1, No.55, 8 Sept 2016 (Legislative Dept, e-Gazette)
second_source: Same Act, copy hosted by the GST Council

claim: Compensation Act: s.3 projected nominal growth of revenue subsumed for a State is fourteen per cent per annum during the transition period; s.4 base year is the financial year ending 31 March 2016; s.6 projected revenue = base-year revenue grown at that rate (illustration: 100 (1+14/100)^3 for 2018-19); 'transition period' is five years from a State's transition date.
source: GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 (Act 15 of 2017, assent 12 Apr 2017), text on CBIC GST site
second_source: Same Act, PDF on the GST Council site

claim: Compensation Act s.7: compensation is payable to a State in the transition period, provisionally calculated and released every two months and finally for each year on figures audited by the CAG; total compensation = projected revenue minus actual revenue (State tax net of refunds + IGST apportioned + other taxes of the State), and any excess released is adjusted next year.
source: GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 (Act 15 of 2017, assent 12 Apr 2017), text on CBIC GST site
second_source: Same Act, PDF on the GST Council site
note: The brief said s.7 holds the 14%/2015-16; the 14% is in s.3 and the base year in s.4. s.7 holds the calculation.

claim: Compensation Act s.8: a cess is levied on specified intra- and inter-State supplies (Schedule) 'for a period of five years or for such period as may be prescribed on the recommendations of the Council'; not leviable on composition-scheme suppliers; the rate is capped by the Schedule.
value: cess for 5 years or as prescribed
source: GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 (Act 15 of 2017, assent 12 Apr 2017), text on CBIC GST site
second_source: Same Act, PDF on the GST Council site

claim: Compensation Act s.10: cess proceeds go to a non-lapsable GST Compensation Fund forming part of the public account of India; all compensation 'shall be paid out of the Fund'; at the end of the transition period 50% of the unutilised balance goes to the Consolidated Fund of India and 50% to States in proportion to their State GST revenue in the last year; the Fund is audited by the CAG.
source: GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 (Act 15 of 2017, assent 12 Apr 2017), text on CBIC GST site
second_source: Same Act, PDF on the GST Council site

claim: Rationale put to the 41st Council: the Joint Secretary (DoR) recalled the Chairperson's remarks at the 7th and 8th meetings that compensation should come from the cess, not the Consolidated Fund, and that the Council would decide if it fell short; he detailed s.10 (compensation released only from the Fund) and the Finance Secretary stressed the Act was passed under the 101st Amendment s.18 for five years. Punjab's Minister recalled that the Finance Ministry told the Standing Committee no loss was expected but the Centre assured compensation; Punjab said States gave up 70-80% of their tax rights.
source: Minutes of the 41st GST Council meeting, 27 Aug 2020 (GST Council)
page_or_section: Agenda Item 1, paras 4-5 (PDF pp.1-5); Punjab remarks p.5 and p.15
note: This is the Department's account of the legislative history in a Council meeting, not the Act. The Act's own rationale is the long title (-01) and the 101st Amendment s.18 (-02). OCR text noisy; page refs approximate. [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Old text said GST was intended to be revenue neutral at best and gave the Finance Secretary the s.10 point. Neither is in paras 4-4.5: s.10 was the JS (DoR); no phrase on revenue neutrality found in the minutes.

claim: Position at 27 Aug 2020 (Joint Secretary, DoR): since 1 July 2017 about Rs 3 lakh crore of compensation had been released against a similar amount of cess collected; the fund balance on 31 July 2020 was about Rs 11,000 crore; after the 14 March 2020 meeting about Rs 65,000 crore was released to States while cess collected in April-July 2020 was about Rs 21,000 crore; the protected revenue grows 14% 'irrespective of how the revenue performs'.
value: gap between protected revenue and cess
source: Minutes of the 41st GST Council meeting, 27 Aug 2020 (GST Council)
note: Quote 'irrespective of how the revenue performs' is from the minutes text (OCR).

claim: Attorney General's opinion read to the 41st Council: the States' entitlement 'is very hard coded in the Act' (protected revenue minus actual revenue, every year); no express provision obliges the Government of India to raise resources; the Council has power to find other sources; the Council may discuss borrowing, but borrowings are governed by Article 293 of the Constitution.
value: legal opinion: entitlement fixed, source unspecified
source: Minutes of the 41st GST Council meeting, 27 Aug 2020 (GST Council)
note: Opinion was sought after the 14 March 2020 Council meeting (para 4.5-4.6); the separate opinion of 26 Aug 2020 on extending the cess is described in the 42nd minutes (-13). The full opinions are annexures to the minutes (Annexure 4), not read.

claim: Estimate presented at the 41st meeting: protected revenue for April-January 2020-21 Rs 6,38,339 crore; if there were no COVID and 10% growth, post-settlement SGST would have been Rs 4,73,161 crore, a shortfall of Rs 1,65,718 crore for ten months against Rs 1,75,000 crore for all of 2019-20; the JS (DoR) put the ten-month gap 'attributable to the implementation of GST' at about Rs 1,65,178 crore (as read); with Rs 11,438 crore in the Fund (31 July 2020) and an estimated Rs 57,266 crore of cess to come, Rs 68,700 crore would be available, leaving a shortfall of Rs 96,477 crore from GST implementation alone.
value: Rs 96,477 crore from GST; rest from COVID
source: Minutes of the 41st GST Council meeting, 27 Aug 2020 (GST Council)
note: OCR numbers: Rs 1,65,718 crore (para 27.2) and Rs 1,65,178 crore (para 27.4) differ by a possible digit transposition; re-check against the PDF page images before printing either. The Rs 96,477 crore result follows from 1,65,178 - 68,700. Total requirement ~Rs 3,00,000 crore against ~Rs 70,000 crore expected cess (paras 27.5, 47). [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Page image of p.44 read: para 27.2 prints Rs 1,65,718 crore, para 27.4 prints Rs 1,65,178 crore. Arithmetic 6,38,339 - 4,73,161 = 1,65,178, so 27.2 carries a printed digit transposition; use 1,65,178. 27.4 also prints 68,700 (11,438 + 57,266 = 68,704) and 96,477; use as printed, labelled approximate.

claim: Finance Minister's (Chairperson's) two options at the 41st Council: Option 1 - a Special Window of borrowing for the GST-implementation shortfall (about Rs 97,000 crore), repaid from the cess extended beyond five years, plus 0.5% of State GDP extra open-market borrowing; Option 2 - borrowing of about Rs 2,30,000 crore (about 1.15% of GDP) for 2020-21, repaid from cess beyond the transition period. In both, borrowing is 'in the name of the States'.
source: Minutes of the 41st GST Council meeting, 27 Aug 2020 (GST Council)
note: The 'in the name of the States' sense is the Chairperson's clarification at paras 49 and 61 (minutes). [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Para 46 prints the Option 1 GST-implementation shortfall as Rs 96,477 crore; the round Rs 97,000 crore is from the 42nd minutes para 33.

claim: State responses at the 41st meeting (as recorded): West Bengal said Option 2 for a limited period, with the Centre borrowing, would be agreeable; Tamil Nadu would go with Option 2 for 2020-21; Puducherry with Option 2 subject to Home Ministry approval; Rajasthan said its fiscal deficit and debt were already beyond FRBM limits and the Centre should borrow and recover from the cess; Kerala said States should be given time to examine; Assam and West Bengal asked for seven working days; the Chairperson said a note on both options would go to States and they would reply within seven working days.
source: Minutes of the 41st GST Council meeting, 27 Aug 2020 (GST Council)
note: Each speaker is named by State in the minutes, as 'Hon'ble Member from'. Names of ministers are not given in the text read; the attendance list is annexed.

claim: Extension of cess: Council (42nd meeting, 5 Oct 2020) took the Attorney General's note of 26 Aug 2020, that the cess could continue beyond five years only if there was a shortfall during the transition period; Kerala, West Bengal, Punjab, Karnataka, Puducherry, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Goa and Odisha welcomed it; the Council 'approved to extend the levy of Compensation Cess beyond June 2022 till the entire shortfall is covered', to be reviewed from time to time.
source: Minutes of the 42nd GST Council meeting, 5 and 12 Oct 2020 (GST Council; OCR text noisy)
page_or_section: Agenda Item 9, paras 26-27 (PDF pp.24-25; printed pp.23-24 of 93)
note: Punjab asked that the end date not be defined (para 26.2). [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Page fixed to PDF pages; verified.

claim: 42nd meeting: the States had been given two options; 21 States opted for Option 1 (23 States/UTs by 12 Oct), none for Option 2, and 8 States had reservations against both (12 Oct). The Department of Expenditure modified Option 1: assumed growth cut from 10% to 7%, raising the amount from Rs 97,000 crore to about Rs 1.1 lakh crore; interest on the borrowing is the first charge on the cess Fund.
source: Minutes of the 42nd GST Council meeting, 5 and 12 Oct 2020 (GST Council; OCR text noisy)
page_or_section: Agenda Item 9A, para 28 (PDF p.26); paras 32-33 (PDF p.43; printed p.42)
note: Count differs between 5 Oct (21 States) and 12 Oct (23 States/UTs): both read in the minutes. 'Puducherry would accept Option 1 if all States did'. [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Pages fixed. Rs 97,000 crore to 1.1 lakh crore is in para 33; para 28.1 gives only the 1.1 lakh crore.

claim: Dissent recorded at the 42nd meeting: the Minister from Punjab said the options were not in accordance with law and that Article 279A(11) provided a dispute resolution mechanism that could be activated, with a division if no consensus; Chhattisgarh supported a division and said its State agreed to neither option; the Minister from Kerala disputed that Option 1 was the Council's decision; West Bengal's Minister said a third option, written to the Prime Minister by its Chief Minister, was for the Union to borrow from the RBI window and credit the Compensation Fund.
value: dissent: Punjab, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, West Bengal
source: Minutes of the 42nd GST Council meeting, 5 and 12 Oct 2020 (GST Council; OCR text noisy)
note: Named by State and as the minutes record them. A Chief Minister's letter to the Prime Minister was reported by the West Bengal Minister, not read. [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Verified. Para 29.17 (Puducherry: no consensus, not agreeing to Option 1) also on p.41.

claim: The other side (42nd meeting): Assam's Minister said about 21 States had 'no dispute with the Centre' and a dispute mechanism was not a priority; Bihar's Deputy Chief Minister (as he recalled, Chairman of the Empowered Committee) said a dispute authority had been rejected earlier by the Standing Committee and perhaps Parliament since States were sovereign, and that Groups of Ministers (11 so far) were the Council's route; Gujarat's Deputy Chief Minister said delay would hurt States not the Centre.
source: Minutes of the 42nd GST Council meeting, 5 and 12 Oct 2020 (GST Council; OCR text noisy)
page_or_section: Assam para 28.24 (PDF p.35); Bihar para 29.4 (PDF p.38); Gujarat para 29.21 (PDF pp.41-42)
note: Paragraph for the Uttar Pradesh remark not isolated; check the page before printing. [Audit 11 Nov 2026] FAIL on original: the dispute-authority remark was attributed to Uttar Pradesh; it is Bihar (para 29.4). Corrected.

claim: The Union Finance Minister told the Council she acknowledged the States' 'desperate financial need' as front-liners against Covid, and that though compensation cess collection was only Rs 96,000 crore the previous year the Centre had released Rs 1,60,000 crore of compensation.
source: Minutes of the 42nd GST Council meeting, 5 and 12 Oct 2020 (GST Council; OCR text noisy)
note: Chairperson's own statement. Compare PIB status note (Rs 1.65 lakh crore for 2019-20).

claim: The Special Window, announced by PIB on 15 Oct 2020: the Centre borrows the estimated shortfall (Rs 1.1 lakh crore if all States join) in tranches and passes it to States as a back-to-back loan in lieu of cess releases; this has no impact on the Centre's fiscal deficit and the amounts are capital receipts of States; it also authorised additional open-market borrowing of 0.5% of GSDP.
source: PIB, Ministry of Finance: Special Window to States for meeting the GST Compensation Cess shortfall, 15 Oct 2020

claim: Borrowing and release figures: Centre borrowed and released Rs 1.1 lakh crore in 2020-21 and Rs 1.59 lakh crore in 2021-22 as back-to-back loans 'to meet a part of the shortfall in cess collection'; PIB (31 May 2022) said 'All the States have agreed' to that decision and Centre released the entire compensation payable up to 31 May 2022, Rs 86,912 crore, though only about Rs 25,000 crore was in the Fund; compensation for June 2022 alone would remain.
source: PIB, Ministry of Finance: Centre Clears Entire GST Compensation Due Till Date, 31 May 2022
second_source: PIB, Ministry of Finance: Status Note on GST compensation released to States/UTs, 27 Apr 2022
note: Ministry's own account. 'All the States have agreed' is the Ministry's statement; the 42nd minutes show formal dissent in Oct 2020 by several States.

claim: Rajya Sabha reply of 7 Dec 2021: pandemic lowered GST and cess collections, so compensation need rose; Rs 1,13,464 crore from the Fund was released for April 2020-March 2021; Rs 37,134 crore (2020-21) and Rs 14,664 crore (April-September 2021) were pending; the issue was deliberated in the 41st, 42nd and 43rd Council meetings; the Minister said the Centre was committed to full compensation by extending the cess.
source: PIB, Ministry of Finance: Payment of GST compensation to States in times of COVID-19 pandemic (Rajya Sabha reply), 7 Dec 2021

claim: Status note of 27 April 2022: Rs 2.78 lakh crore of compensation released for 2020-21 including loans, nothing pending for 2020-21; for 2021-22 Rs 78,704 crore pending 'due to inadequate balance in the fund'; Rs 7.35 lakh crore released in all.
source: PIB, Ministry of Finance: Status Note on GST compensation released to States/UTs, 27 Apr 2022

claim: The transition period and compensation end: the Compensation Act's cess period is 'five years or such period as may be prescribed'; the CBIC/DGTS flyer says the cess would be collected 'till 1st July 2022'; PIB (31 May 2022) said only compensation for June 2022 remained due to be paid.
source: PIB, Ministry of Finance: Centre Clears Entire GST Compensation Due Till Date, 31 May 2022
second_source: CBIC/DGTS flyer 'GST Compensation Cess' (on GST Council site), 5 Aug 2019
note: Compensation (not cess) ended with June 2022 (the five years from 1 July 2017). The Fund and cess continued, to repay the borrowings (-13, -23). [Audit 11 Nov 2026] Flyer file is from the GST Council site (publisher not stated in text); it says till 1st July 2022. The statement that compensation ended with June 2022 is our reading of the Act's five-year transition period (s.2(1)); PIB says only that June 2022 would remain.

claim: Current position: the monthly GST report for March 2026 says 'Compensation cess is continuing only as a transitory arrangement till entire loan and interest liability are discharged'. Domestic cess was Rs 98,708 crore and import cess Rs 6,015 crore for FY 2025-26, but only Rs 103 crore domestic and nil on imports in March 2026.
source: GSTN/GST Council: GST Gross and Net Collections as on 31/03/2026
second_source: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1430, 9 Feb 2026, Ministry of Finance (Dept of Revenue)
note: Cess collection in 2024-25 was Rs 1,53,302 crore (Lok Sabha reply 1430).

claim: 56th Council (3 Sept 2025): changes in GST rates were phased because of 'the requirement of funds to fulfill the obligation under the compensation cess account'; pan masala, gutkha, cigarettes, chewing tobacco, unmanufactured tobacco and bidi kept existing GST and compensation cess until the loan and interest are completely discharged.
source: PIB / GST Council: Recommendations of the 56th GST Council meeting, 3 Sept 2025
